findings: Proof of 1° (l.424–428): it says the support of U' is supplementary to « le support L de U ». That needs span(L ∩ W) = L. This holds when W spans E (any element of span W is r(w₁ − w₂), and w₁, w₂ then lie in one fibre), but the printed proof does not argue it. The formalized proof needs neither span(L ∩ W) = L nor W spanning E: it takes L' = span U' plus a supplementary of L ⊔ span U'. This is a gap in the proof, not an error in the statement.
The proof's two lemmas (l.430–431, l.445–446) hold for a NONEMPTY convex C. U = L ∩ W always contains O, so the proof is not affected. Formalized as eq_zero_of_vadd_subset and eq_zero_of_vadd_eq.
questions: Prop. 3 is read with Déf. 3's standing hypotheses on W (convex, containing O, spanning E), because « fibre cylindriquement » is defined only for such W. With this reading 2° is exactly the print. 1° is proved without spanning. Without spanning, 2° is false: point_deux_conjugues.

labels.label: bzdef:c3s2d4_conjugues
questions: Déf. 4 (l.415–418) prints only W = L ∩ W + L' ∩ W, with no supplementarity. Formalized as printed (SontConjugues). As printed it admits non-supplementary pairs even for W convex, spanning, with no line: ℝ is conjugate to itself relative to [0, ∞[ (demiDroite_conjugues_non_supplementaires). Three passages point to the supplementary pair IsCompl L L' ∧ SontConjugues W L L' of Prop. 3 2°: « Cette proposition légitimera la » (l.413), Théorème 1's « couples de sous-espaces distingués conjugués » with projections P_L parallel to L', and Théorème 2's « on prend comme complémentaire le conjugué ». Both forms are available, and conjugue W L is the supplementary one. Downstream targets (T-bz-c3-conjugues, T-bz-c3-boole-affine) should use the supplementary pair. Whether Déf. 4 should be read with « supplémentaires » is the author's reading to give.

instances.what: in the cube [−1,1]ⁿ (any n) every coordinate subspace coord S is distinguished, and its conjugate is coord Sᶜ, the only supplementary L' with W = L∩W + L'∩W (by Prop. 3 2°: cube_hyps gives convex, 0 ∈, spanning, no half-line)
the same for [−1,1]³, the block's instance
in the closed unit ball of any real inner product space, L is distinguished iff L = ⊥ ∨ L = ⊤ (parallelogram law on unit vectors u ∈ L, ±v ∈ L')
the only subspaces fibring the closed ball are ⊥ and ⊤ (Prop. 3 1°, the ball being bounded)
in the strip ℝ × [0,1] (convex, 0 ∈, spanning, contains a line) the horizontal axis has two different conjugates, the vertical axis and the diagonal: 2°'s no-line hypothesis is used
the cone {|x| ≤ y} (convex, no line, contains half-lines) is fibred by the vertical axis but not cylindrically: 1°'s no-half-line hypothesis is used
{0} ⊂ ℝ² (no line, not spanning): two conjugates of the horizontal axis, so 2° uses spanning
Déf. 4 as printed: ⊤ conjugate to ⊤ relative to [0,∞[ ⊂ ℝ, with ⊤, ⊤ not supplementary

kb_proposals: Chapter3/Fibres: the predicates Fibre, FibreCylindriquement (= EstDistingue) and SontConjugues contain the condition only. The standing hypotheses (convex, 0 ∈ W, span W = ⊤) are theorem hypotheses. For the supplementary pair use IsCompl L L' ∧ SontConjugues W L L', and conjugue W L for the chosen conjugate (conjugue_eq and conjugue_conjugue need convex, 0 ∈ W, spanning, no line).
Destructuring x ∈ s + t after `rw [h]`, where h unfolds a def into a Minkowski sum, leaves a beta-unreduced `(fun x1 x2 => x1 + x2) a b`. Write `rw [h, Set.mem_add] at hx` before obtain/rintro.
The span of a convex C ∋ 0 is ℝ₊(C − C): exists_smul_sub_of_mem_span (Chapter3/Fibres), by Submodule.span_induction.
